desc:
You may delete one contiguous block of elements from nums (the block may be empty). After the deletion, the remaining elements, in their original order, must be sorted in non-decreasing order.

Return the smallest possible length of the deleted block.

nums = [2, 4, 9, 3, 1, 5, 6]
delete [9, 3, 1] -> [2, 4, 5, 6]
result = 3

nums = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
result = 4      (keep any single element)
hints: What do the elements you keep look like? They form a prefix and a suffix of the original array, and both must already be sorted.
Find the longest sorted prefix and the longest sorted suffix first. Which blocks are candidates if you keep only one of them?
To keep part of both, use a pointer i in the prefix and j in the suffix. If nums[i] ≤ nums[j] you can join them (delete j - i - 1 elements) and advance i; otherwise advance j.
editorial: Whatever remains is a prefix nums[0..i] plus a suffix nums[j..n-1]. Each must be non-decreasing by itself, so i is at most the end l of the longest non-decreasing prefix and j is at least the start r of the longest non-decreasing suffix. Also the join must be valid: nums[i] ≤ nums[j].

If the array is already sorted the answer is 0. Otherwise the answers that keep only a prefix or only a suffix cost n - l - 1 and r. For the combined case, sweep: with i = 0 and j = r, if nums[i] ≤ nums[j] record j - i - 1 and increase i (a longer prefix is better for this j); otherwise nums[j] is too small for this and every larger prefix end, so increase j. Both pointers only move forward, so the sweep is O(n).
